scope: Broaden PAR-126 semantic review to ordered multi-content cells, content-indexed block attributes, and linked cell-range behavior; refine implementation readiness without enabling unsupported output.

method.kind: Read-only Autodesk managed API research plus local first-party source and existing test-vector review
localInspection: DRW_TableCell stores ordered m_contents and cell-level m_attributes; DRW_TableCellAttribute has ATTDEF handle/index/text but no owning content ordinal.
parseTableCell appends ATTDEF tuples inside each content loop and marks such content semantically incomplete.
dxfRW::writeTable currently requires exactly one content matching the coarse cell type; its output admission remains narrower than the in-memory content vector.

Existing generated parser and adapter cases cover a one-block-content attribute profile and a separate multi-content FIELD/value profile, but not attributes associated with a later block content in the same cell.
Prior PAR-126 work remains uncommitted in the pre-existing dirty checkout; no source files were changed in this research pass.
method.evidenceRule: ODA v5.4.1 controls serialized DWG/DXF field order. Autodesk managed API docs are semantic cross-checks only and do not establish byte layout, object ownership, producer validity, native refresh success, or libdxfrw support.

evidence.observed: Autodesk LinkedTableData says a cell can contain multiple ordered contents with value, field, or block data; Cell.Contents provides access to all contents, and Table.CreateContent adds content beyond the one created by default.
doesNotEstablish: DWG/DXF serialization order or exact content type values
that every possible content combination is supported by libdxfrw or AutoCAD consumers
evidence.planUse: Preserve ordered DRW_TableCell::m_contents; keep one-content DXF writer admission explicit until expanded and tested.

evidence.observed: Autodesk's Table.GetBlockAttributeValue(row,column,contentIndex,attDefId) explicitly takes the content ordinal; CellContent exposes block-attribute methods. Local parsing consumes ATTDEF tuples inside the per-content loop, but the local model stores them in a flat cell-level vector without that ordinal.
doesNotEstablish: whether the ODA tuple index is the ATTDEF ordinal or a content ordinal
evidence.planUse: Add explicit owning-content association while retaining the ATTDEF index independently. Create generated controls with a non-block content before an attribute-bearing block content. Verify exact ODA semantics and producer bytes before claiming support.

evidence.topic: DATALINK range semantics and refresh boundary
evidence.observed: Autodesk Cell.GetDataLinkRange reports the linked range containing a cell; range-based SetDataLink binds a DataLink object to cells and can reject an overlapping range. The DataLink class manages connection information to an external source, and update is a distinct operation.
doesNotEstablish: ODA BL93/BL94 per-cell consistency rules or link-range encoding
TABLECONTENT/DATALINK owner, NOD, extension-dictionary, or DXF root edges
external spreadsheet path resolution or refresh behavior after conversion
evidence.planUse: Require producer-backed wire and owner/range census before enabling linked export. Track stored metadata/object graph preservation separately from live source resolution/update.

evidence.topic: Current local model and output boundary
evidence.observed: The model captures ordered cell contents but flat ATTDEF tuples do not record their source content slot. The parser already marks attribute-bearing content incomplete. The DXF writer admits exactly one matching cell content, so the identified association issue is a latent model-completeness gap rather than current false-success or silent writer loss.
doesNotEstablish: current producer compatibility or complete AC1021/AC1024+ TABLE support
that generic API success proves linked or multi-content semantics
evidence.planUse: Refine PAR-126/7G.3d.3b-c; no new finding is needed. Keep attribute-bearing and linked profiles incomplete until data model, graph closure, serializer, and independent evidence are complete.
